Web design in Kilgore, TX has an unusual brief. Kilgore had 13,376 residents at the 2020 census, mostly in Gregg County with the rest in Rusk, yet people across the country have heard of its oil derricks and its Rangerettes. That means a Kilgore business is selling to three crowds at once: the people who live here, the oil and gas companies that never left, and the visitors who come for a game, a show or the lights. Dominion Web Design Pro writes sites that work for all three, page by page, and shows you a free demo before you pay.

The Kilgore calendar, from a business owner's side

Most small towns have one big weekend. Kilgore has visitors spread across the year, and each group finds its way around the same way: on a phone.

WhenWhat brings people inWhat they search for
FallKilgore College football and the Rangerettes at halftimePlaces to eat before the game, hotels for visiting families
Late November into JanuaryThe downtown derricks lit with stars, which earned Kilgore the official title City of StarsDinner, gifts, holiday hours, things to do downtown
Late June and JulyThe Texas Shakespeare Festival at Kilgore CollegeRestaurants near campus, lodging, somewhere open after a show
All yearStudents and staff at Kilgore College, oil field crews and vendorsRepairs, haircuts, apartments, supplies, food

None of those people have a neighbor here to ask. If your restaurant, salon, shop or repair business does not come up when they search, they never learn it exists, and the visiting half of your market is the half that can grow.

Oil built Kilgore, and it still shapes who buys from you

On October 3, 1930, "Dad" Joiner's Daisy Bradford No. 3 came in on a Rusk County farm and set off the East Texas oil boom. Kilgore sat in the thick of it. Wells crowded so tightly into downtown that one plot of about 1.2 acres became known as the World's Richest Acre, and today it is a park among the steel derricks that still stand over the middle of town.

The boom faded, but the industry did not leave. Oil and gas service companies, machine shops, trucking outfits and supply houses still work out of Kilgore. They sell to other businesses, and for them a website does a different job: it is the background check a buyer runs before picking up the phone. A plain page listing your services, your equipment and your service area does more there than any slogan.

A college sits in the middle of town

Kilgore College is the other engine. In 1939 the college hired Gussie Nell Davis, and in September 1940 her Rangerettes gave their first performance, and they are widely described as the first women's precision dance and drill team. The Rangerettes are still the college's calling card, and the summer Texas Shakespeare Festival, which the college started in 1986 for the Texas Sesquicentennial, brings a theater crowd to campus every June and July.

For a business, a college means a population that turns over every year. Each fall a new group of students and their parents arrive knowing nothing about where to eat, where to get a phone screen fixed or which apartment manager returns calls. They have never heard your name from a neighbor. They search, read two or three sites, and choose. The businesses near campus that have a clear site and an accurate map listing get that choice; the ones that rely on everybody already knowing them do not.

The same goes for the families who drive in for a Rangerette performance or a weekend of plays. They plan dinner and a place to stay from a hotel room or a parking lot, often an hour before they need it, so a site that loads quickly and shows hours and a phone number at the top is worth more to them than any amount of design polish.

Two kinds of Kilgore website, built the same honest way

For businesses that sell to the public

Restaurants and barbecue, boutiques downtown, salons and barbers, mechanics, contractors. The site needs your hours front and center, seasonal changes posted early, directions that make sense to a stranger, and a number that dials with one tap. The $497 Starter site covers that.

For businesses that sell to other businesses

Oil field service, fabrication, hauling, industrial supply. The site needs a page per service, the counties you cover, and enough detail to show you are established. The $997 Pro site, with 10 city pages for places like Longview, Henderson, Overton and White Oak, usually fits better.

Both get the same treatment: every page written by hand for your business, a contact form that emails you every lead, titles, descriptions and a sitemap submitted to Google, and a site you own outright. The $1,997 Agency build adds keyword research across your whole territory and a page for every town and service worth having. See the pricing page for every detail, including the optional AI agents.

Free help for Kilgore owners

Kilgore falls inside the territory of the UT Tyler-Longview Small Business Development Center, which gives free advising to businesses in Gregg and Rusk counties and four more around them. Business plans, loan applications and cash flow are their everyday work. The Kilgore Area Chamber of Commerce on North Kilgore Street is the local network for introductions and referrals. We have no arrangement with either one; they are simply worth a call before you spend money on anything.

What we will not tell you

We will not tell you a new site will put you first on Google, or bring a set number of calls. Nobody honest can promise that. What we can say is that the groundwork will be done right: fast pages on a phone, a clear title and description on each one, schema markup, a sitemap, and copy that names Kilgore and the towns around it in plain words. Reviews on your map listing and time do the rest. You can see what your current site is missing with the free Site Check.

Common questions

Who can build a website for my Kilgore business?

Dominion Web Design Pro, run by Maurice Johnson from Big Sandy in neighboring Upshur County. He writes every page himself and builds a free demo of your site before you are asked to buy anything.

How do I get visitors in Kilgore for the Christmas lights to find my shop?

Get the site live well before Thanksgiving, list your holiday hours plainly, describe where you are relative to downtown, and keep your Google Business Profile matched to the site. The lit derricks run from the first Saturday after Thanksgiving until after New Year's Day, and people plan those evenings on their phones.

Does an oilfield service company in Kilgore need a website?

Yes, though for a different reason than a cafe. Buyers in the oil and gas business check out a vendor before they call: what you do, what equipment you run, what area you cover, and whether you look established. A clean site with a page for each service answers those questions before the first phone call.

What does web design cost in Kilgore, Texas?

With us it is a one-time price: $497 for Starter, $997 for Pro, $1,997 for Agency. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI chat or phone agent. The website itself is paid for once, with no payment plan.

Can you update my Kilgore website when my hours change for the holidays?

Yes. Updates are part of hosting and maintenance, which is $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. Send the new hours by email or text and they go on the site. Changing your Google Business Profile to match is worth doing the same day.
